pois.description: A square frame with a circle cut out of the middle stacked on a triangular frame with circles cut out of each side. The top piece used to rotate, but has since been secured by the artist for safety of public and artwork.
pois.name: Changing Form
pois.owner: City of Seattle Office of Arts & Culture

kerry-park.name: Kerry Park viewpoint
kerry-park.blurb: A small terrace on Queen Anne Hill with Seattle's postcard view: the Space Needle in front of the downtown towers, Elliott Bay to the right and Mount Rainier behind on clear days.

spawn.note: At the railing beside Changing Form, facing the Needle.

extent.description: The 1.26-acre park strip along W Highland Dr between 2nd and 3rd Ave W: sidewalk, lawn terrace, railing edge, Changing Form sculpture, stairs west down to W Prospect St and Bayview-Kinnear Park (playground). Highland Dr mansions as the north backdrop.
extent.edges: Railing/steep slope south; W Highland Dr north (parked cars).
extent.vertical: Park at ≈104 m (USGS EPQS 103.8 m at the viewpoint); Space Needle base ≈40 m, so its top (≈224 m) appears ~5.3° above the eye; slope falls ~60 m to Mercer St.

columbia_center.note: directly behind the Needle — the classic stack

rainier.note: right of the Needle by ~11°; summit 4,392 m; visible only on clear days (render as a separate far billboard/mesh with atmospheric fade)

elliott_bay.note: bay, West Seattle, ferries; Bainbridge Island and Olympic foothills to the W/SW

view_composition.method: bearings/distances computed from coordinates (great-circle); elevations from USGS EPQS and OSM

structures.name: Changing Form (Doris Totten Chase, 1971)
structures.form: Abstract steel sculpture: a square frame with a circular hole stacked on a triangular/curved base, smooth black curves; hollow so kids crawl through; photographers frame the skyline through the circle.
structures.copyright_note: 1971 artwork by Doris Totten Chase — stylise.

signage.where: park sign near W Highland Dr
signage.style: Seattle Parks brown sign with white letters (verify)

vegetation: Lawn strip, a few shrubs; big trees and hedges of the Highland Dr mansions behind; downslope tree canopy partly framing the view

lighting.day: Backlit skyline in the afternoon (looking SE, sun from SW → side light); morning sun behind the city
lighting.night: Classic blue-hour shot: city lights + Needle floodlit; Great Wheel LED show visible

backdrop: 1:1 downtown skyline at 1.5–4 km (low-poly city impostor), Space Needle at 1.28 km detailed enough for a 50 mm lens
Elliott Bay with ferries and container cranes (Harbor Island)

crowd.density: Low by day (5–20), packed at sunset and for fireworks (NYE Needle fireworks); tour buses pull up on Highland Dr.

plaques.title: A gift of the view
plaques.text: Albert S. and Katharine Kerry donated the land in 1927 "so that all who stop here may enjoy [its] view."

plaques.title: Changing Form
plaques.text: Doris Totten Chase's 15-ft steel sculpture (1971) is a favourite frame for photographers and a jungle gym for kids.

plaques.title: On screen
plaques.text: Kerry Park's view opens 10 Things I Hate About You and is the view from Frasier's apartment.

interaction.primary: "The Mountain is out": weather-dependent Rainier visibility — the postcard challenge requires Needle + Rainier in one frame (only possible on clear days in real weather, spec 18).
secondary: Frame the skyline through Changing Form's circle

iconic.frame: Space Needle centred-left, Columbia Center stack behind, Rainier to the right, at blue hour

seasonal: Clear Rainier views most often July–Sept; winter days often hide it

dialogueGeneral.usage: Pedestrian set for the Seattle and Bellevue driving districts and as filler in every spot. ctx: greeting|bumped|photographed|idle|spot|rain|honked_at|near_miss; non-English lines carry orig+lang with English text.

tone.note: "Seattle Freeze": locals are described as "very polite but not particularly friendly" to strangers — keep local NPC lines courteous, brief, low-key; few unprompted chats.
Washington ranked 48th of 50 states for extraversion (2008 study cited by Wikipedia) — locals default to nods, "sorry", "you're good".

Honking is rare and seen as rude: ~3 in 4 Northwest drivers said they rarely or never honk (PEMCO 2017); attitudes softened by 2021 (65% say honking at least somewhat appropriate). NPC reaction to player honking near spots: surprised/disapproving, not aggressive.
Coffee culture: Seattle drinks more coffee than any other US city; espresso small talk is a safe icebreaker.
Rain talk is universal small talk; locals rarely use umbrellas (hoods/rain shells) — common local self-image, unsourced folklore: keep light.

Visitors: Canada was 73% of Seattle's 2.4 M international visitors in 2024; then China, India, UK, South Korea, Germany, Japan, Australia, France, Taiwan — languages used: English, French (Québec), Mandarin, Hindi, Korean, German, Japanese, Spanish (domestic + Latin America).
Indigenous art (totems, Salish Welcome): staff/guides speak respectfully; no jokes about sacred objects.
Guardrails: no stereotypes, accents written phonetically, slurs, politics or alcohol jokes about any group; tourists are curious and happy, locals helpful-but-reserved.
